title: A Escarpment for the Horizon
premise: Zephyrine Sterling, a storm chaser hiding from creditors in a river town, is blackmailed into joining a rescue mission for an expedition that went silent upriver. She finds the survivors guarding a discovery that could ruin them all: proof of a pre-colonial settlement the expedition's financier wants erased and sold. As the dry season shrinks the river and the financier's hired men close in, Zephyrine must choose between paying her debt with silence or burning her last chance at safety to bring the truth home. She chooses justice, loses the money, and finally gains a place among the people she once watched from a distance.
about_author: Marguerite Voss is the pen name of a former field researcher who spent six years documenting remote river communities before turning to fiction. Her work explores how landscapes remember what people try to forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Weather
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Chasing a storm on the escarpment to film footage she can sell, she's intercepted by Odile Brant, who holds her debt and offers a deal: join the rescue mission for the vanished Halvorsen expedition, or face the optimists she owes. The beat is reluctant commitment—she takes the job because invisibility has failed her.

chapters.title: Six Days of Static
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with radio logs interspersed. Aboard the rescue boat with a skeleton crew—a skeptical pilot, a medic, and Odile's quiet enforcer Tomas—she reconstructs the expedition's final transmissions. The emotional beat is unease: the logs suggest the team stopped answering not from disaster, but by choice.

chapters.title: Where the River Forgets Its Name
chapters.summary: Pilot Amara Okonkwo's POV. The crew passes the last mapped tributary into unmapped water, and old river families refuse to guide them further, warning of 'the place that keeps its people.' Zephyrine's competence earns grudging respect, but the beat is isolation—the deeper they go, the more alone they are.

chapters.title: Smoke Without a Fire
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They find the expedition's abandoned camp: equipment intact, food untouched, and a journal page describing stone terraces older than any known civilization. The beat is dread shifting to wonder—something made these people stay, and it wasn't danger.

chapters.title: The People Who Kept Their People
chapters.summary: Medic Yusuf Adeyemi's POV. They find the expedition alive at a hidden settlement, healthy but refusing rescue. The archaeologist Halvorsen shows them the terraces—and reveals the financier funded the dig specifically to destroy the evidence and sell the land rights. The beat is moral vertigo: the rescue was always a cover story.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Silence
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Odile orders the crew to report nothing found and help clear the site; in exchange, Zephyrine's debt vanishes. Tomas, himself once bought this way, privately urges her to take the deal. The beat is temptation—freedom offered at exactly the price of her conscience.

chapters.title: What the Dry Season Takes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The river drops faster than forecast, stranding the boats and forcing everyone—crew, expedition, and settlement descendants—to shelter together as Odile's second team arrives upstream with demolition permits. The beat is forced intimacy; enemies become neighbors around one fire.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. With the river too shallow for the main boat, Zephyrine proposes moving everyone and the evidence overland through the escarpment caves—a route only the settlement elders know. The beat is fragile alliance: trust extended across generations of grievance, with Odile's men one ridge behind.

chapters.title: Terrace of Bones and Light
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Ambushed at the cave mouth, she trades herself to Odile's enforcers to buy the others time, then turns the tables using a storm she's tracked all week—luring the mercenaries onto the exposed flats before the flash flood. The climax: Halvorsen's records survive, Odile's operation drowns in paperwork and scandal, and Zephyrine nearly drowns saving the last child.

chapters.title: An Escarpment for the Horizon
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, months later. Debt-free but broke, she declines a lucrative contract to keep silent and instead testifies alongside the settlement's descendants as the site gains protection. The resolution: she stays in the river town—not invisible anymore, but seen, belonging at last to people who know exactly what she did and chose her anyway.
